text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
- IG Metall metallworkers union wants to place emphasis of its efforts in the future on job security. Wage rises should be limited to matching inflation rates.
- Unemployment rate in Germany in September down slightly
- CDU parliamentarian calls for long-term reductions in pension payments and raising pension age to 67 from 65
- Finance Ministry gives into pressure from government coalition in the dispute over valuations for inheritance tax
- IG Metall: jobs more important than wages
- SPD not ready to make any compromises on child support money or capital gains taxation
- IG Metall wants to make job security for members top priority
- Wage committee at Labour Ministry puts off decision setting minimum wage for construction workers
- Hardly any improvement in German unemployment rate

- Taxes: efforts to reform tax system causing tension in government coalition. FDP chairman Wolfgang Gerhardt complains bitterly about coalition partner CSU to small group of party leaders. CSU leader Michael Gros lashes out at FDP.
- European court rules that German government has to reimburse holiday-makers whose trips were interrupted by bankruptcy of MP Travel Line tour operator
- German President Roman Herzog awards 71 federal medals of honour
